answer: A concrete Sybil defense is per-identity staking tied to a scarce resource. Each agent locks a bond that scales with how many attestations it issues, and every attestation is signed and scored against independent evidence. To spin up N identities an attacker must post N bonds, and any identity caught faking loses its bond. Since bond cost sits above the payout of a sybil set, copying one agent into an atlas of clones stops paying, and a forged horizon of fresh accounts costs more than it yields. One detected fake also voids the glacier of attestations it backed.
